newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian PM Mahathir endorses deputy as successor.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian PM Mahathir endorses deputy as successor.

text.p: Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad endorsed his deputy, Anwar Ibrahim, as his eventual successor after a magazine hinted at a conspiracy to topple Anwar, the national Bernama news agency said on Friday.
"I will abide by the wishes of the party, which has chosen...Anwar as my successor, and I am giving him 100 percent support," Bernama quoted Mahathir as saying.

The two men have often been viewed as potential rivals for the leadership of the United Malays National Organisation (UMNO), the dominant member of the ruling coalition, in party elections set for 1999.

Mahathir was re-elected president of UMNO last month and has not said whether he will run again in the next party elections in 1999. Both Mahathir and Anwar, who is party deputy president, were unchallenged at the triennial elections.
Asiaweek magazine reported in its November 15 issue that Anwar's political future was being threatened by the return of Tengku Razaleigh Hamzah, a former rival of Mahathir.

Razaleigh recently disbanded his opposition Spirit of 46 party to rejoin UMNO. Asiaweek named several party leaders as sympathetic to Razaleigh, saying their support could help him challenge Anwar in the 1999 party elections.

UMNO elections are traditionally viewed as more important than national polls because the party has handily won every election since 1957, and its president and deputy president have always been Malaysia's prime minister and deputy prime minster.
Mahathir described the Asiaweek article as "pure speculation" to boost sales of the magazine.
He said Razaleigh had returned to UMNO as an ordinary member and no conditions were attached.
